retrieval_ledger.snippet: Most states allow this after a local election official confirms that the absentee/mail ballot has not already been returned or counted.

| State | Citation | Summary |
| Alabama | Alabama Code § 17-10-2. | If a voter has requested, but not voted by absentee ballot, the voter may cast a provisional ballot. |
| Alaska | Alaska Division of Elections | A voter who requests an absentee by-mail ballot but decides to vote early or in-person on Election Day instead must destroy and dispose of the absentee ballot before voting. |
| Arizona | Ariz. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 16-579 | A qualified elector who has applied for an early ballot but has not voted and will not vote for that early ballot, or who surrenders the early ballot to the precinct inspector on Election Day, may vote in person according to the procedures in A.R.S. § 16-584. If an electronic pollbook or similar system is used, and it shows the early ballot has not been returned or accepted, the voter may be issued a standard ballot after presenting identification. If the system shows the early ballot has been received or accepted, the voter may only be issued as a provisional ballot. |
| Arkansas | Ark. Stat. Ann. § 7-5-411 | Any person to whom an absentee ballot is delivered according to the precinct voter registration list, but who elects to vote by early voting or to vote at his or her polling site on Election Day, shall be permitted to cast a provisional ballot. |
| California | Cal Elec Code § 3015; § 3016; § 3016.5 | Voters must surrender their vote by mail ballot to the inspector of the precinct board, a member of the vote center election board or the elections official to be permitted to vote on a nonprovisional ballot in person. If voters are unable to surrender the vote by mail ballot, they may still vote a nonprovisional ballot if the election officials verify that the vote by mail ballot has not been returned and notate the voter’s record to ensure the vote by mail ballot is not cast or tabulated after the in-person vote. If neither of these conditions are satisfied, the voter must be issued a provisional ballot. |
| Colorado | Colo. Rev. Stat. § 1-7-303; § 1-7-110 | Any eligible elector who spoils a ballot may obtain another ballot, not exceeding three in total, by returning each spoiled ballot to the election of judges at the polling place or voter service and polling center. The spoiled ballots are immediately canceled and preserved for return to the designated election official. This process does not prohibit an elector from obtaining a replacement ballot.  An eligible elector who is unable to produce identification may cast a provisional ballot. |
| Connecticut | Connecticut Secretary of State | If a voter has requested, but has not returned the absentee ballot prior to Election Day, the voter may vote in-person on Election Day. |
| Delaware | Delaware Department of Elections | If a voter requests, but does not return, a vote-by-mail ballot, the voter may vote in person. |
| Dist. of Columbia | District of Columbia Board of Elections | All voters receive a mail ballot. A voter may choose to vote in person instead. If the pollbook shows voters have received an absentee ballot for the election and have not already voted, a special ballot will be counted. |
| Florida | Fla. Stat. § 101.69; § 101.048; § 104.17 | An elector who has received a vote-by-mail ballot and has not returned it to the supervisor but wishes to vote in person must return the ballot, whether voted or not, to the election board at the precinct or to an early voting site, where it will be marked “canceled” and placed with other canceled ballots. If the elector does not return the ballot and the election official confirms that the supervisor has received the elector’s vote-by-mail ballot, the elector is not allowed to vote in person. If the elector maintains that the vote-by-mail ballot has not been returned or remain eligible to vote, the elector must be provided with a provisional ballot.  Any person who willfully votes or attempts to vote both in person and by vote-by-mail ballot at any election is guilty of a third-degree felony. |
| Georgia | Ga. Code § 21-2-38;  Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 183-1-14-.06 | An elector who has requested an absentee ballot and wishes to vote by a different method instead may surrender the absentee ballot to the poll manager at the assigned precinct or an early voting site. Upon surrendering the absentee ballot, the elector will be permitted to vote on a regular ballot in person. The poll manager will mark the surrendered absentee ballot as “Canceled” with the date and time, initial and make appropriate notations beside the elector’s name on the electors list. All canceled absentee ballots are returned with other ballots to the superintendent. |
| Guam | 6 GAR § 1242; 3 GCA Section 9137; 3 GCA Section 9138; 6 GAR § 1304; 6 GAR § 1303 | When a voter returns a ballot that has been issued but not voted on, the precinct's board must treat it as a spoiled ballot. The ballot must be cancelled by drawing a large "X" at least 3 inches across its face, with the official writing "returned unmarked by voter" on it, and then the ballot must be placed in the ballot box.  If a voter spoils a ballot, it may be returned to a member of the precinct board, and the voter may receive another ballot, up to a maximum of three. The precinct board must immediately cancel the spoiled ballot by writing an "X" on its face, count and seal all spoiled ballots in an envelope marked "Spoiled Ballots" and return them to the Election Return Center at the close of polls.  If an absentee ballot is received but the voter has voted in person, the precinct board must reject the absentee ballot. |
| Hawaii | Hawaii Rev. Stat. § 11-105; § 15-5 | If a voter needs a replacement ballot because the original was destroyed, spoiled or lost, the voter may request a replacement from the clerk, who will verify that another ballot has not been returned by the voter before issuing the replacement. If multiple absentee ballots are returned for the same election, only the first absentee ballot that is not spoiled will be prepared for counting. |
| Idaho | Idaho Code § 34-1006 | If a voter who requests an absentee ballot chooses to vote in person instead, the voter must bring the absentee ballot to the polls.  Every elector shall always be provided with the opportunity to vote in person in an election. |
| Illinois | 10 Ill. Comp. Stat. § 5/18A-5(a)(6); § 5/17-9  Illinois State Board of Elections | A voter who has already received a mail ballot must take it to an early voting site or polling place on Election Day and surrender it to an election judge. The mail ballot will be voided, and the voter will receive a regular ballot.  A person who claims to be a registered voter is entitled to cast a provisional ballot if the voter received a vote-by-mail ballot but did not return it to the election authority. |
| Indiana | Ind. Code § 3-11.5-4-18; § 3-11.5-4-13(f) | A voter who has received an absentee ballot in Indiana must return the ballot to the inspector before being permitted to vote in person. The returned absentee ballot will be marked “canceled” and preserved with the rejected ballots. If the voter has requested but not received an absentee ballot, the voter may vote in person after executing an affidavit affirming nonreceipt of the absentee ballot.  The absentee ballot counters or county election board shall issue a certificate to a voter whose ballot has been rejected under this section if the voter appears in person before the board not later than 5 p.m. on Election Day. The certificate must state that the voter’s absentee ballot has been rejected and that the voter may vote in person. |
| Iowa | Iowa Code § 53.19 | A registered voter who has received an absentee ballot and not returned it may surrender the absentee ballot to the precinct officials and vote in person at the polls. The precinct officials must mark the uncast absentee ballot “void” and return it to the commissioner.  If confirmation cannot be made, the voter must cast a provisional ballot. |
| Kansas | Kan. Stat. Ann. § 25-1122f; § 25-1136 | If an advance voting ballot is destroyed, spoiled, lost or not received by the voter, the voter may request a provisional replacement ballot from the county election officer.  If a voter’s advance voting ballot is challenged or otherwise determined to be invalid, the ballot envelope is marked “provisional,” and the validity of the ballot is determined by the special election board. |
| Kentucky | Ky. Rev. Stat. § 117.085 | When a voter who has requested a mail-in absentee ballot does not receive it within a reasonable amount of time, the voter must contact the county clerk, who will issue another mail-in absentee ballot. The county clerk is required to keep a record of all mail-in absentee ballots issued and returned, as well as in-person absentee voting, to ensure that only the first voted ballot is counted. If a mail-in absentee ballot is returned after the first one has already been returned, the county clerk must mark the outer envelope of the subsequently returned ballot with the words “Canceled because ballot reissued.” |
| Louisiana | La. Rev. Stat. § 18:1305; § 18:1311(E); § 18:562(B)(1) | Voters who appear during early voting or on Election Day and are not on the list of voters who have already voted early or returned a mail ballot may cast a regular ballot at their precincts. |
| Maine | Me. Rev. Stat. Ann. tit. 21, § 759 | The warden is required to write “Rejected” on the absentee ballot envelope, state the reason and initial it if the voter has voted in person. |
| Maryland | Md. Election Law Code Ann. § 9-311.1; COMAR 33.11.05.04; COMAR 33.16.06.04 | When a voter who has permanent absentee ballot status in Maryland wishes to receive an absentee ballot by a different method from the one previously indicated, the voter must notify the local board of elections of this change.  If a voter submits both an absentee ballot and a provisional ballot, the local board will count the first ballot cast if it is legally sufficient and will reject any subsequent ballot from the same voter; if an absentee ballot is received after a provisional ballot from the same voter has already been counted, the absentee ballot will be rejected. |
| Massachusetts | 950 CMR 54.04 | If any person who has been sent an absentee ballot tries to vote in person at the election, precinct officers should see the letters AV or SAV opposite his name on the voting list. This person must present a certificate obtained from the city or town clerk authorizing him to vote in person. The city or town clerk shall by telephone authorize the presiding officer to issue such certificate if the clerk determines that a voter at the polling place is entitled to it, and the presiding officer shall then sign and issue the certificate. The presiding officer shall securely attach the certificate to the voting list and duly note that the voter in fact voted in person. If no certificate is authorized, election officers must refuse to let the person vote and they shall refer the voter to the city or town clerk. |
| Michigan | Mich. Comp. Laws § 168.765b; § 168.769 | An elector who has returned an absent voter ballot may, before 5 p.m. on the second Friday before an election, appear in person at the city or township clerk’s office, submit a signed, written statement requesting to have the absent voter ballot spoiled, and vote a new absent voter ballot in the clerk’s office.  If an absent voter did not receive an absent voter ballot applied for, or lost or destroyed the ballot, and wishes to vote in person on Election Day, the voter must sign an affidavit to that effect before an election inspector and will then be allowed to vote in person, subject to challenge. |
| Minnesota | Minn. Stat. § 203B.081;  Minnesota Secretary of State | Voters who have requested a mail ballot may appear to vote in person during early voting or on Election Day and cast a regular ballot as long as their mail ballot has not been received and counted by election officials. |
| Mississippi | Miss. Code Ann. § 23-15-637; CMSR 01-000-170 (2.3) | If an absent elector appears at the polling place on Election Day, after having been mailed an absentee ballot or returned an absentee ballot and seeks to cast a regular ballot, the voter must be informed that he/she is not entitled to cast a regular ballot, but the voter may cast an affidavit ballot. The absentee ballot, upon receipt by the registrar, processed as received in SEMS and deposited into a secure ballot box, shall be final, if accepted by the Resolution Board. |
| Missouri | Mo. Rev. Stat. § 115.655 | If a voter has destroyed, spoiled, lost or not received an absentee or mail-in ballot, the voter may obtain a replacement ballot by signing a verified statement and delivering it to the election authority before noon on Election Day. The election authority will then provide a replacement ballot, keeping a record of each replacement issued. |
| Montana | Mont. Code Ann. § 13-13-204 | An elector who has received but not voted an absentee ballot may appear at the appropriate polling place on Election Day and vote in person after being issued a provisional ballot. |
| Nebraska | Neb. Rev. Stat. § 32-949.01; § 32-942 | If a registered voter in Nebraska has received an early voting ballot that is destroyed, spoiled, lost or not received, the voter may either cast a provisional ballot at the polling place on Election Day or obtain a replacement ballot by signing a statement, on a form prescribed by the secretary of state, affirming the original ballot was destroyed, spoiled, lost or not received and delivering it to the election commissioner or county clerk.  A voter who chooses to vote at the polling place on Election Day, rather than by early voting, must do so at the polling place assigned to the voter’s precinct unless returning a ballot for early voting or voting pursuant to specific statutory exceptions. |
| Nevada | Nev. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 293C.26316; § 293.269917; NAC 293C.155; NAC 293.243 | If a mail ballot has been sent to a voter who wishes to vote in person instead, the voter must either surrender the mail ballot at the polling place or sign an affirmation under penalty of perjury stating that he or she has not voted during the election. Any surrendered mail ballot must be marked “Cancelled” by the person receiving it. If voters indicate that they elected not to receive a mail ballot or did not receive one, they are not required to surrender a mail ballot or sign an affirmation before voting in person. |
| New Hampshire | New Hampshire Election Procedure Manual | If a voter brings an absentee ballot in person to the polling place on Election Day, the voter must be instructed to vote in person using an Election Day ballot. The voter must turn in the  absentee ballot, and election officials must reject that ballot, preserve it unopened and mark "voted in person" on the unopened ballot. The rejection reason must be entered into SVRS. |
| New Jersey | N.J. Rev. Stat. § 19:63-20 | If a person has applied for a mail-in ballot but has not received it, or has received it but not transmitted it to the county board or given it to a bearer for delivery before the polls open, that person may vote in person by provisional ballot at the polling place in the assigned election district on Election Day. If the voter appears at the polling place without the mail-in ballot and wishes to vote, that person may also vote by provisional ballot. |
| New Mexico | N.M. Stat. Ann. § 1-6-16 | A voter who has been issued a mailed absentee ballot but whose voted ballot has not been received by the county clerk as of Election Day may go to a voter convenience center and, after executing an affidavit stating the wish to void any previous mailed ballot issued, shall be permitted to vote by another method.  If the county clerk has begun the process of qualifying mailed ballots and the voting location does not have real-time synchronization between the voting location and the qualification of mailed ballots, the voter must cast a provisional ballot. The ballot will be counted once officials confirm no other ballot from the voter has been processed in that election. |
| New York | NY CLS Elec § 9-209 | If the central board of canvassers determines that a person was entitled to vote at such election, the board shall cast and canvass such affidavit ballot if such board finds that the voter appeared at a polling place, in the correct county, which is designated as a polling place for the correct assembly district. |
| North Carolina | North Carolina State Board of Elections | Voters may still vote in person as long as they do not return their absentee ballot. Their absentee ballot will be spoiled after they vote in person. They may simply discard their absentee ballot. There is no need to bring it with them to a polling place. |
| North Dakota | North Dakota Secretary of State’s Office | Voters who received an absentee ballot but choose to vote in person instead will be issued a new ballot at their polling location. |
| Northern Mariana Islands | Not specified. | Not specified. |
| Ohio | Absentee Voting Directive 2023-27, Ohio Secretary of State; Ohio Rev. Code Ann. § 3511.13 | If a voter previously submitted an absentee ballot application for a mailed ballot and appears for early in-person voting, the voter does not need to vote provisionally, as long as no other provisional reasons apply. If a registered elector appears to vote and that elector has requested or cast a uniformed services or overseas absent voter’s ballot for that election, the elector shall be permitted to cast a provisional ballot. |
| Oklahoma | Okla. Stat. tit. 26, § 7-115 | If registered voters have requested an absentee ballot, they shall be required by the judge to sign an affidavit swearing or affirming that they have not cast such an absentee ballot and are entitled to vote in person. |
| Oregon | Or. Rev. Stat. § 254.480; § 253.065 | An elector may obtain a replacement absentee ballot if the original ballot is destroyed, spoiled, lost or not received by completing and signing a replacement ballot request form. The request may be made electronically, by telephone, in writing, in person or by other means designated by the secretary of state by rule [1][2]. |
| Pennsylvania | Pa. Stat. tit. 25, § 3146.6 (b) | An elector who requests an absentee ballot and who is not shown on the district register as having voted the ballot may vote by provisional.  An elector who requests an absentee ballot and who is not shown on the district register as having voted the ballot may vote at the polling place if the elector remits the ballot and the envelope containing the declaration of the elector to the judge of elections to be spoiled and the elector signs a statement subject to the penalties. |
| Puerto Rico | Not specified. | Not specified. |
| Rhode Island | R.I. Gen. Laws § 17-20-25; § 17-20-29 | Every voter who has received a mail ballot and has not cast it shall nevertheless return the unvoted ballot and its uncertified enclosing envelope to the state board or local board with a statement that the voter is not using the mail ballot, before 8 p.m. on Election Day.  Any person whose name has been marked on the voting list may also be permitted to vote in person if that person executes and delivers to the local board an affidavit stating that the person did not receive the mail ballot, or that the mail ballot was lost or destroyed. |
| South Carolina | S.C. Code Ann. § 7-15-430 | A voter who is provided an absentee ballot, but who has not returned an absentee ballot, may cast a provisional ballot at that voter’s resident precinct or at an early voting center in that person’s county. The provisional ballot must only be counted if the absentee ballot is not received by the closing of the polls on Election Day. |

retrieval_ledger.title: Voting at a Polling Place after Applying to Vote by Mail
retrieval_ledger.snippet: Even if you receive your vote-by-mail ballot, you can change your mind and vote at a polling place on Election Day. To do so, you can: Mark your ballot and ...
retrieval_ledger.page_text:
Even if you receive your vote-by-mail ballot, you can change your mind and vote at a polling place on Election Day. To do so, you can:

* Mark your ballot and seal it inside the mailing envelope provided by your county elections official. Be sure to sign and date the outside of the envelope in the space provided. Then bring the sealed envelope to any polling place in your county, or to your county elections office between 7:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. on Election Day.

### OR

* Bring your unused vote-by-mail ballot to your local polling place anytime between 7:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. on Election Day and give it to a poll worker, who will exchange it for a polling place ballot you can use instead.

If you do not bring your vote-by-mail ballot with you, you will not lose your opportunity to vote at a polling place on Election Day. A poll worker will provide you with a provisional ballot, which will be counted after your county elections official has confirmed you are registered to vote in that county and did not vote more than once in that election.
